The assertion failed because `encode.build(types,m,{"a":1},True)` returns n=2 (params + result) but plan["variables"]=3 (includes the flag). My dev encoder's `build` appends the flag when `flag is not None` — here I passed `result=True` and no flag, so n=2. Let me fix the test: use `encode.build(types,m,{"a":1},True,flag)` which appends the flag.

Actually for raw flag bytes I want to control the byte value, so let me build without the flag and append manually, and assert n == variables - 1.

cd /workspace/dev && python3 - <<'PYEOF'
import sys, json
sys.path.insert(0,'/workspace/dev')
import kit, encode
types=[{"name":"Bool","kind":"bool"},{"name":"B","kind":"int","bits":8}]
mods=[{"name":"f","params":[["x","B"]],"result":["o","Bool"],"requires":None},
      {"name":"e","params":[["a","B"]],"result":["r","Bool"],"requires":None}]
pipes=[{"target":"e","filter":"f","bind":{"x":"a"}}]
camp={"types":types,"modules":mods,"calls":[],"pipes":pipes,"entries":["e"],"machine":None,"runs":[]}
plan=kit.run(camp)["plans"][0]
m=mods[1]
def mk(a,flag_bytes):
    objs,n=encode.build(types,m,{"a":a},True)
    assert n==plan["variables"]-1, (n, plan["variables"])
    return kit.encode(objs+[('x2',flag_bytes)])
camp["runs"]=[{"entry":"e","ktest":mk(1,b'\x00')},   # filter requires null -> accepts -> flag 0 -> READY
              {"entry":"e","ktest":mk(1,b'\x01')},   # flag mismatch -> INVALID
              {"entry":"e","ktest":mk(1,b'\x02')},   # flag leaf range -> INVALID
              {"entry":"e","ktest":mk(1,b'\x00\x00')}]# flag width -> INVALID
out=kit.run(camp)
print(json.dumps(out["records"]))
PYEOF
